newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally, end strong on bottom-fishing.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally, end strong on bottom-fishing.

text.p: Mexican stocks ended strong as foreign and domestic buyers stepped into the Mexican market to snap up bargain stocks in late trade.

"We think this is a good time to acquire positions in the market, and investprs seem to also," said Daniel Romo, equity analyst at the Bancomer brokerage. "They're beginning to buy on favorable expectations fro quarterly reports."
The blue chip IPC index closed up 50.16 points, or 1.55 percent, at 3,286.48. Volume picked up after midsession, particularly in blue chips, and stood 89.1 million shares for the session.

Traders noted the presence of market heavyweights like brewers Grupo Modelo and steelmakers Hylsamex on the percentage gainers' list, after several days in which infrequently traded stocks had come to the fore.
"The market had brought blue chips down to support levels, and that's where buyers stepped in, as with Modelo and Hylsamex," an equity analyst said.

Another notable gainer was holding company Grupo Carso whose A1 series stock closed up 1.40 pesos to 36.00 pesos on news that its telecommunications subsidiary was to increase its capital by 682.5 million pesos.
A total of 108 stocks changed hands on the broad market, with winners outnumbering losers 49 to 35.

Technical analysts meanwhile said the rally was partly due to oversupply of paper and the fact that the IPC had validated support at 3,200 points. The rally will hinge on whether it can be sustained by volume.

"This was all spurred by short-term investment. If the rally continues and breaks the 3,300-point mark, that would be a buying signal, but it would need to be validated by volume," said a technical analyst.
